item.title: SpaceX’s Starship nails a smooth return with historic catch
item.description:
SpaceX is preparing for a historic first with the launch and retrieval of the largest and most powerful rocket ever built. Starship Flight 15 is set to take off on Friday from Starbase in South Texas in a monumental attempt to catch both stages of the rocket on its return to Earth. What makes this particular launch so significant is the attempt to retrieve both parts of the rocket: the Super Heavy first-stage booster and upper-stage Starship, also known as “Ship,” which will be caught in back-to-back landings using the launch tower’s “chopstick” arms. The 15th flight for the megarocket, which also plans to deliver 26 new Starlink V3 satellites into orbit, will be granted a 75-minute launch window opening at 5:45 p.m. ET. item.title: Democrat wins Alaska governor’s seat for first time in nearly 30 years
item.description:
Democrat Cindy Holscher is projected to become the next governor of Kansas, marking the first time the state will have two women governors back-to-back, according to Decision Desk HQ. In addition to the governorship, Democrats will also hold a Senate seat in Kansas — the first time that’s happened since the 1930s — as the blue wave that overtook the country this Election Day washes over the state. With Holscher’s victory, Democrats have now won three straight gubernatorial elections in Kansas, which has not happened since 1974. But the race was extremely close and wasn’t called until Thursday. The Democratic state senator defeated Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson. Holscher will replace term-limited Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly. item.title: Israel kills Hamas commander in strike on Gaza camp, officials say
item.description:
Throughout Israel’s war on Palestine, doctors Thaer Ahmad and Feroze Sidhwa spent months at Nasser Hospital in the southern Gaza city of Khan Younis, where they provided care as volunteers and survived a raid and an airstrike on the complex. On Wednesday evening, they were in an Uber in New York headed to a screening of their film about their time in Gaza when they realized Nasser was the target of another Israeli airstrike. “They just hit Nasser again,” Ahmad said, turning from the front seat toward Sidhwa. “I think Rizk is dead.” He was referring to Dr. Rizk Abu Shaaira, an experienced surgeon and fixture of the Palestinian medical community whom both had worked alongside at the hospital and who appears in their film “ American Doctor .” When Israel attacked Nasser Hospital on Wednesday — for at least the seventh time since the genocide escalated in 2023 — Abu Shaaira was one of the…

item.title: Video shows moment of Brooklyn building collapse from inside
item.description:
Six adults and two children were killed Wednesday afternoon when a three-story building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue collapsed into a construction site next door. Eighteen other people were injured in the collapse or responding to it. One of them remains in critical condition, Mayor Zohran Mamdani reported at a press conference Thursday afternoon. Many of the people impacted by the collapse are immigrants, the mayor said, including from Trinidad, Colombia and Mexico. One victim was a 26-year-old father from Ecuador, Today reported . José Luis Caguana Cosquillo leaves behind his pregnant wife and their first child. Two of the people killed were construction workers working on the excavation next door at the time of the collapse, City officials said. item.title: Democrats fumbled the Hegseth impeachment. That could be a blessing in disguise | Claire Finkelstein
item.description:
Most of America bemoans political gridlock in the nation’s capital. DC area commuters deplore the city’s transit gridlock. But Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth may now be a fan of DC’s legendary traffic snarls. It appears that crosstown traffic may have prevented him from becoming only the third Cabinet secretary ever impeached by the House of Representatives. The House voted 211-204 this week to divert an effort by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) to impeach Hegseth. House Republicans moved to block a straight, up-or-down vote on impeachment. Instead, Republicans forced a vote on sending the articles to the Judiciary Committee. That’s where they’d go to die. If the House failed to sidetrack the articles, Members would have then voted on actual impeachment. If a simple majority voted to impeach, Hegseth would join 19th century Secretary of War William Belknap and former Homeland Security Secretary…

item.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
item.description:
The AI boom without Jensen Huang will test a hard truth: Even if the tech world has grown somewhat less reliant on Nvidia's chips, it remains highly dependent on its checkbook. Why it matters : With rival chips maturing and recent software breakthroughs, the tech ecosystem has achieved what would've seemed impossible a year ago: a viable path around Nvidia. But replacing a CEO willing to bankroll startups, backstop billions in cloud debt and aggressively fund rivals to the AI giants will be much harder. item.title: Beijing faces its Russia dilemma amid talk of Xi-Trump-Putin summit
item.description:
‘We think dialogue is a good thing,’ Australian PM says after German chancellor urges the US to work with Europe for peace in Ukraine Australia has endorsed this week’s historic summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in China, even as European leaders warn that the US president must not make major concessions over the war in Ukraine. The three-way summit is planned to take place in Shenzhen, where the leaders will gather for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting. Likened to the 1945 summit at Yalta , the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has warned the talks must not lead to a redistribution of influence among world powers or the abandonment of his country, more than four years into the war sparked by Putin’s full-scale invasion.
